issues.legal_issue: A temporary injunction in a suit for specific performance requires a strong prima facie case on undisputed facts, satisfaction of the other injunction requirements, and fair conduct by the applicant.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought temporary injunctions in suits for declaration and specific performance of alleged agreements to sell land.
The courts below granted and affirmed injunctions restraining dealings with the land.
issues.conclusion: A plaintiff seeking temporary injunction in a suit for specific performance must establish a strong prima facie case on undisputed facts. The court must also consider irreparable injury, balance of convenience, and the applicant’s conduct, exercising its discretion judicially.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 36 and 37 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 provide for preventive relief and make temporary injunctions subject to the Code of Civil Procedure. Under Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh, a prima facie case alone is insufficient: irreparable injury and a balance of convenience in favour of relief must also be shown. Motilal Jain v. Ramdasi Devi, Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co., and M.P. Mathur v. DTC establish that delay, the applicant’s conduct, mutuality, and the equitable nature of the remedy are relevant. Wander Ltd. v. Antox India P. Ltd. states a rule of prudence for appellate interference, dependent on the facts of the case.

rule.if: temporary_injunction_in_specific_performance_case and (not strong_prima_facie_case or not irreparable_uncompensable_harm or not balance_favors_applicant or not fair_applicant_conduct)

predicates.temporary_injunction_in_specific_perform: A plaintiff sought an interim restraint in a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.strong_prima_facie_case: The applicant produced undisputed facts establishing a strong prima facie basis for the claim.
predicates.irreparable_uncompensable_harm: The applicant faced material harm that could not be adequately compensated by damages or another remedy.
predicates.balance_favors_applicant: The likely harm from refusing relief outweighed the likely harm from granting it.
predicates.fair_applicant_conduct: The applicant acted fairly and was not responsible through fault, delay, or inequitable dealings for the situation complained of.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance case seeking interim restraint, the injunction should be refused if the applicant lacks any one of a strong prima facie case, irreparable uncompensable harm, a favourable balance of convenience, or fair conduct.

issues.legal_issue: An interim injunction was unsustainable where the available material did not establish a concluded agreement prima facie and the claimant’s delay allowed the opposing parties to materially change their position.
material_facts: The negotiations included repeated exchanges of emails and messages, and the documents continued to be revised.
The claimant knew that the land was being negotiated for sale with other prospective purchasers and knew that its own negotiations had virtually fallen through.
The claimant’s purported acceptance was received after the opposing parties had proceeded with another sale, and the claimant’s advance was refunded.
The claimant did not promptly retransfer the refunded advance and filed suit about seven months later.
Before the suit was filed, the alternative purchaser had made substantial payments and the opposing parties had used a substantial part of the proceeds, materially changing their position.
issues.conclusion: The existence of a concluded contract remained a matter for trial, but the claimant had not shown on the admitted facts that the parties were ad idem or that execution of a written agreement was merely a formality. In light of the claimant’s delay and the intervening change of position, the balance of convenience favoured the opposing parties, and the injunctions were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Agriculture Produce Market Committee, Gondal v. Girdharbhai Ramjibhai Chhaniyara supports treating prolonged negotiations as remaining at an embryonic stage where mutual assent is not established. Under Brij Mohan v. Sugra Begum, the party asserting a concluded agreement bears the onus of showing that the parties were ad idem and had discharged their obligations. Madamsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yelloji Rao and Mandali Ranganna v. T. Ramachandra explain that discretionary relief may be refused where a claimant’s conduct or neglect induces a prejudicial change of position or makes relief inequitable. Delay within the limitation period may still matter where third-party rights have accrued or the circumstances make discretionary relief inequitable, as explained in Motilal Jain.

rule.if: interlocutory_specific_performance_case and negotiations_unresolved_on_available_material and claimant_knew_of_parallel_negotiations and acceptance_followed_alternative_sale and claimant_delayed_after_refund and opposing_parties_materially_changed_position

predicates.interlocutory_specific_performance_case: A claimant sought an interim injunction while pursuing specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.negotiations_unresolved_on_available_mat: The available communications showed continuing negotiations and did not establish mutual assent to all material terms.
predicates.claimant_knew_of_parallel_negotiations: The claimant knew that the opposing parties were negotiating the same transaction with other prospective purchasers.
predicates.acceptance_followed_alternative_sale: The claimant communicated purported acceptance after the opposing parties had proceeded with a transaction with another purchaser.
predicates.claimant_delayed_after_refund: After learning of the competing transaction and receiving a refund, the claimant did not promptly retransfer the money and waited before bringing suit.
predicates.opposing_parties_materially_changed_posi: Before suit was brought, the opposing parties received substantial payments and used proceeds, while the competing purchaser made substantial investments.

issues.definition: When an interim specific-performance claim rests on unresolved negotiations, the claimant knew of parallel negotiations, purported acceptance followed an alternative sale, the claimant delayed after a refund, and the opposing parties materially changed their position, the injunction should be set aside.
